title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第35部分：数据库

chapters.Codd: 1. 问要什么，而不是怎么做
chapters.OurDb: 15. 我们的数据库运行任务
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

fc14f8c36b2b.en: For thirty parts the Job has been a program: tokenize the novels, count the words in a hash table, sort, print the top twenty. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every step of it chosen by hand, with the data structure, the hashing and the sort each a part of this course. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is the same job as one line of SQL. It says what we want: for each word, how many times it occurs, the twenty most common. It says nothing about how. <bookmark mark='c'/> Loaded into a database as four point six million rows, one per word, it gives exactly the same twenty answers, <bookmark mark='d'/> and sqlite, on this machine, answers in about two seconds, with no instructions at all about hash tables or sorts.
fc14f8c36b2b.zh: 三十个部分以来，任务一直是一个程序：把小说切成词，用哈希表计数，排序，打印前二十名。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一步都是手工选定的，其中的数据结构、哈希和排序，各自都是这门课的一个部分。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是同一个任务，写成一行 SQL。它只说想要什么：每个词出现了多少次，最常见的二十个。它完全不说怎么做。<bookmark mark='c'/>把小说装进数据库，成为四百六十万行，每个词一行，它给出完全相同的二十个答案，<bookmark mark='d'/>而 sqlite 在这台机器上大约两秒就答完了，关于哈希表或排序，一句指示也没有。

5eade411d7e8.en: So who decides how? <bookmark mark='a'/> A database turns the query into a plan in stages. The parser reads the SQL; the optimizer considers many plans that would all give the right answer, and estimates what each would cost; the executor runs the cheapest. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is the plan our own database, built for this part, chose for the Job: scan the words, aggregate them in a hash table, and keep the top twenty in a heap. It found Part 17's program by itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> And underneath is a second machine, the transaction manager, which lets thousands of users read and write at once, each as if alone, even through crashes.
5eade411d7e8.zh: 那么，由谁来决定怎么做？<bookmark mark='a'/>数据库分几个阶段把查询变成计划。解析器读入 SQL；优化器考虑许多都能给出正确答案的计划，估计每个的代价；执行器运行其中最便宜的那个。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是我们为这一部分自己搭建的数据库为任务选的计划：扫描所有词，在哈希表里聚合，再用一个堆保留前二十名。它自己找到了第17部分的程序。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在下面还有第二台机器，事务管理器，它让成千上万的用户同时读写，每个人都仿佛独自在用，即使经历崩溃也一样。

c967a4869f0e.en: This is Part 35 of Computer Science, Built: Databases. <bookmark mark='a'/> We start with Codd's idea and the algebra it created, and the theory of good table design. We follow a query through iterators and joins, measuring their costs, and watch an optimizer search for the cheapest plan, and see why its estimates go wrong. We build a B-plus tree. Then transactions: what it means for concurrent work to be correct, how locking and snapshots achieve it, and what the weaker isolation levels give up. Then recovery with ARIES, column stores for analytics, and our own database running the Job.
c967a4869f0e.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第35部分：数据库。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们从 Codd 的想法和它所创造的代数开始，再讲好的表设计的理论。我们跟着一个查询走过迭代器和连接，测量它们的代价，看一个优化器搜索最便宜的计划，并弄清它的估计为什么会出错。我们搭一棵 B+ 树。然后是事务：并发的工作怎样才算正确，锁和快照如何做到这一点，较弱的隔离级别又放弃了什么。然后是用 ARIES 做恢复、面向分析的列存储，以及我们自己的数据库运行任务。

437664ba6a74.en: Chapter one. Ask for what, not how.
437664ba6a74.zh: 第一章。问要什么，而不是怎么做。

b3781e7b5f32.en: The first databases were structures you walked. <bookmark mark='a'/> IBM's IMS, built in the 1960s for the parts lists of the Apollo programme, stored records in a hierarchy: a library holds books, a book holds chapters. The CODASYL standard of 1969 joined records with pointers into a network. <bookmark mark='b'/> A program navigated: get this book; get the next chapter within it; and again, until the status code said there were no more. <bookmark mark='c'/> Every new question was a new program, written by someone who knew the pointers. And if the data was reorganised on disk, for speed, the old programs broke.
b3781e7b5f32.zh: 最早的数据库是要你一步步走过的结构。<bookmark mark='a'/>IBM 的 IMS 建于 1960 年代，为阿波罗计划的零件清单而生，把记录存成层次：图书馆里有书，书里有章。1969 年的 CODASYL 标准则用指针把记录连成网。<bookmark mark='b'/>程序要导航：取这本书；取它里面的下一章；再取，直到状态码说没有了。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个新问题都是一个新程序，得由熟悉那些指针的人来写。而如果为了速度在磁盘上重新组织数据，旧程序就全坏了。

82ae0099a39e.en: In 1970 Edgar Codd, a mathematician at IBM, proposed something else. <bookmark mark='a'/> Users of large shared databases, he wrote, must be protected from having to know how the data is organised in the machine. <bookmark mark='b'/> Data should be relations: sets of tuples, tables, with no pointers and no order. <bookmark mark='c'/> Tables connect through values: a key that identifies a book appears in the rows that refer to it. <bookmark mark='d'/> A query states what the result is, in logic, and the system works out how to compute it. <bookmark mark='e'/> And so the physical design, indexes, layout, the order of rows, can change without changing a single query. <bookmark mark='f'/> Many at IBM doubted it could be made fast. System R and Berkeley's Ingres proved it could, and System R's query language, SEQUEL, became SQL.
82ae0099a39e.zh: 1970 年，IBM 的数学家 Edgar Codd 提出了另一种做法。<bookmark mark='a'/>他写道，大型共享数据库的用户，必须不必知道数据在机器里是怎样组织的。<bookmark mark='b'/>数据应当是关系：元组的集合，也就是表，没有指针，也没有顺序。<bookmark mark='c'/>表通过值相连：标识一本书的键，出现在引用它的那些行里。<bookmark mark='d'/>查询用逻辑说明结果是什么，由系统去想出怎样计算。<bookmark mark='e'/>于是物理设计，索引、布局、行的顺序，都可以改变，而不必改动任何一个查询。<bookmark mark='f'/>IBM 里很多人怀疑这能做得快。System R 和伯克利的 Ingres 证明了可以，而 System R 的查询语言 SEQUEL 后来成了 SQL。

a8a8168d2af4.en: We can watch data independence at work in our own database. Here is a question about the novels: which books use the word whale most? <bookmark mark='a'/> Without an index on the word column, the database must read every page of the words table: twelve hundred pages, on a sample of the corpus. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add a B-plus tree on that column, and the same query, unchanged, reads 85 pages, because the optimizer now finds the whale rows through the index. <bookmark mark='c'/> Moby Dick, of course. The query never mentioned the index. That is Codd's point.
a8a8168d2af4.zh: 我们可以在自己的数据库里看到数据独立性在起作用。这是一个关于小说的问题：哪些书用 whale（鲸）这个词最多？<bookmark mark='a'/>如果词这一列上没有索引，数据库就必须读遍词表的每一页：在语料的一个样本上，一千二百页。<bookmark mark='b'/>在这一列上加一棵 B+ 树，同一个查询，一字未改，只读 85 页，因为优化器现在通过索引找到那些 whale 行。<bookmark mark='c'/>当然是《白鲸》。查询从没提到索引。这正是 Codd 的要点。

08df77742d40.en: Codd gave his model an algebra: operators that each take tables and return a table, so they can be combined freely. Here are two small tables, books and authors. <bookmark mark='a'/> Selection keeps the rows that satisfy a condition: the books published before 1900. <bookmark mark='b'/> Projection keeps some columns, and drops the duplicate rows that may result: the authors. <bookmark mark='c'/> Join pairs every book with every author it agrees with on the shared column: now each book carries its author's year of birth. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the set operations, union and difference, work on tables of the same shape, here the books not in a second list, with renaming to make shapes match. That is all. Every question of the kind SQL asks is a composition of these.
08df77742d40.zh: Codd 给他的模型配了一套代数：每个运算接受表、返回一张表，所以可以随意组合。这里有两张小表，书和作者。<bookmark mark='a'/>选择保留满足条件的行：1900 年以前出版的书。<bookmark mark='b'/>投影保留一部分列，并去掉因此可能出现的重复行：作者。<bookmark mark='c'/>连接把每本书和在共同列上与它一致的每位作者配对：现在每本书都带上了作者的出生年份。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有集合运算，并和差，作用在形状相同的表上，这里是不在第二张清单里的书，再用重命名让形状对上。就这些。SQL 所问的那类问题，每一个都是这些运算的组合。

42f2d05a3989.en: Combining operators gives a tree. <bookmark mark='a'/> Which books did their authors publish before the age of forty-five? Join books to authors, select the rows where the year minus the birth year is under forty-five, and project the titles. <bookmark mark='b'/> In SQL it reads almost like English, and the database translates it back into a tree like this one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Emma, Persuasion and Ulysses qualify; Dracula does not: Stoker was fifty. <bookmark mark='d'/> Codd also showed that the algebra is exactly as expressive as a logic of tuples, the relational calculus, which is closer to how SQL states things. <bookmark mark='e'/> And because operators obey laws, the tree can be rewritten, selections pushed down, joins reordered, without changing the answer. Choosing among those rewritings is the optimizer's job.
42f2d05a3989.zh: 把运算组合起来，就得到一棵树。<bookmark mark='a'/>哪些书是作者在四十五岁以前出版的？把书和作者连接，选出出版年份减出生年份小于四十五的行，再投影出书名。<bookmark mark='b'/>用 SQL 写，读起来几乎像英语，而数据库会把它翻译回这样一棵树。<bookmark mark='c'/>《爱玛》《劝导》和《尤利西斯》符合条件；《德古拉》不符合：斯托克那时已经五十岁了。<bookmark mark='d'/>Codd 还证明了，这套代数与一种关于元组的逻辑，即关系演算，表达能力完全相同，而关系演算更接近 SQL 的表述方式。<bookmark mark='e'/>又因为运算服从定律，这棵树可以改写，把选择往下推，给连接重新排序，而答案不变。在这些改写之中作出选择，就是优化器的工作。

f75e938e61c2.en: Chapter three. Dependencies and normal forms.

c7126c8a85c3.en: Tables can be designed badly. Here is one that records students, their courses, each course's instructor, and the instructor's office. <bookmark mark='a'/> If Codd moves office, three rows must change, and an update that misses one leaves him with two offices. <bookmark mark='b'/> A course that has no students yet cannot be recorded at all, because every row needs a student. <bookmark mark='c'/> And when the last student drops the operating systems course, the fact that Ritchie sits in room w3 disappears with her. <bookmark mark='d'/> These are update, insertion and deletion anomalies, and they all have one cause: the table records several independent facts, and repeats each of them.
c7126c8a85c3.zh: 表也可能设计得很糟。这一张记录了学生、他们的课程、每门课的教师，以及教师的办公室。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果 Codd 换了办公室，就必须改三行，而一次漏掉一行的更新会让他有两个办公室。<bookmark mark='b'/>一门还没有学生的课根本无法记录，因为每一行都需要一个学生。<bookmark mark='c'/>而当最后一个学生退掉操作系统课时，Ritchie 坐在 w3 房间这个事实也随她一起消失了。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是更新异常、插入异常和删除异常，它们只有一个原因：这张表记录了几个彼此独立的事实，而且每个都重复了。

43e0954f59de.en: The theory that names the problem is functional dependency. <bookmark mark='a'/> A course determines its instructor, and an instructor determines an office: wherever two rows agree on the left side, they agree on the right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Armstrong's three axioms derive every dependency that follows from these, and no others. <bookmark mark='c'/> The closure of course is course, instructor and office. <bookmark mark='d'/> A key is a set whose closure is every attribute: here, the student and the course together. <bookmark mark='e'/> Boyce-Codd normal form asks that the left side of every dependency be a key. <bookmark mark='f'/> Course determines instructor and office, but course is not a key, so the table is not in normal form, and that is exactly where the repetition comes from.
43e0954f59de.zh: 为这个问题命名的理论是函数依赖。<bookmark mark='a'/>课程决定教师，教师决定办公室：只要两行在左边一致，它们在右边也一致。<bookmark mark='b'/>Armstrong 的三条公理能推出由这些依赖得出的每一条依赖，而且只推出这些。<bookmark mark='c'/>课程的闭包是课程、教师和办公室。<bookmark mark='d'/>键是闭包为全部属性的集合：这里是学生和课程合在一起。<bookmark mark='e'/>Boyce–Codd 范式要求每条依赖的左边都是键。<bookmark mark='f'/>课程决定教师和办公室，可课程不是键，所以这张表不满足范式，而重复正是从这里来的。

6ebbc2bb5cfa.en: The cure is to decompose. <bookmark mark='a'/> Split the table along the offending dependency, and repeat until every piece is in normal form: instructors and offices; courses and instructors; students and courses. Each fact is now stored once. <bookmark mark='b'/> The split must be lossless: joining the pieces must give back exactly the original rows, and the chase, a mechanical test, confirms it. <bookmark mark='c'/> A careless split, students and courses in one table, students, instructors and offices in another, fails the test: joining them invents rows that were never there. <bookmark mark='d'/> There is a price. Sometimes no Boyce-Codd decomposition keeps every dependency checkable inside one table. <bookmark mark='e'/> The third normal form, built by Bernstein's synthesis, always keeps them, at the cost of a little redundancy, and that is the compromise most designs make.
6ebbc2bb5cfa.zh: 解药是分解。<bookmark mark='a'/>沿着出问题的依赖把表拆开，重复下去，直到每一块都满足范式：教师与办公室；课程与教师；学生与课程。现在每个事实只存一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>拆分必须是无损的：把这些块连接回来，必须恰好得到原来的行，而追逐法，一种机械的检验，证实了这一点。<bookmark mark='c'/>一种草率的拆法，学生和课程放一张表，学生、教师和办公室放另一张，通不过检验：把它们连接起来，会凭空造出从未有过的行。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是有代价的。有时没有任何 Boyce–Codd 分解能让每条依赖都在单张表内检查。<bookmark mark='e'/>用 Bernstein 的合成法构造的第三范式总能保住它们，代价是一点冗余，这也是大多数设计所作的折中。

84abfd53dc1c.en: Chapter four. How a query runs.
84abfd53dc1c.zh: 第四章。查询是怎样运行的。

c9be84e7e66b.en: A plan is a tree of operators, and almost every database runs it the same way. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each operator is an iterator, with three calls: open, next, close. Next returns one tuple, or says there are no more. <bookmark mark='b'/> The root asks its child for the next tuple, which asks its child, down to the scan, which reads a row from a page and passes it up. <bookmark mark='c'/> Tuples flow up one at a time, so the scan never stores the table. <bookmark mark='d'/> Some operators must see all their input before producing anything: a sort, a hash join building its table, an aggregate. <bookmark mark='e'/> Goetz Graefe's Volcano made this the standard model, because any operator can sit under any other.
c9be84e7e66b.zh: 计划是一棵运算符树，几乎每个数据库都用同一种方式运行它。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个运算符都是一个迭代器，有三个调用：open、next、close。next 返回一个元组，或者告诉你没有了。<bookmark mark='b'/>根向它的孩子要下一个元组，孩子再向它的孩子要，一直到扫描，扫描从页里读出一行，往上传。<bookmark mark='c'/>元组一次一个地往上流，所以扫描从不需要存下整张表。<bookmark mark='d'/>有些运算符必须先看完全部输入，才能产出任何东西：排序、正在建表的哈希连接、聚合。<bookmark mark='e'/>Goetz Graefe 的 Volcano 让这成为标准模型，因为任何运算符都可以放在任何其他运算符之下。

9556904a4311.en: Here is the Job's plan from our database, with what happened when it ran. <bookmark mark='a'/> The scan produced four point six million tuples. <bookmark mark='b'/> The hash aggregate folded them into fifty-eight thousand groups, one per distinct word. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the top-twenty operator kept a heap of twenty. <bookmark mark='d'/> The table was read once, forty-six thousand pages; the other plan, sorting the words to group them, was estimated at five times as many page reads, and rejected. <bookmark mark='e'/> Our engine, in Python, took seven seconds; sqlite, in C, two. The answers agree to the last count.
9556904a4311.zh: 这是我们的数据库为任务定的计划，以及它运行时发生了什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>扫描产出了四百六十万个元组。<bookmark mark='b'/>哈希聚合把它们折叠成五万八千个组，每个不同的词一组。<bookmark mark='c'/>前二十名运算符保留了一个大小为二十的堆。<bookmark mark='d'/>表只读了一遍，四万六千页；另一个计划，先把词排序再分组，估计要读五倍的页，因而被否决。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们的引擎用 Python 写，花了七秒；sqlite 用 C 写，两秒。两者的答案一直到最后一个计数都一致。

72e3c9f8a1aa.en: The first choice is how to reach each table: read it all, or use an index. Here is the whale query on a sample of the corpus, three ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> Scan the words and join with nested loops. <bookmark mark='b'/> Scan and hash join: the same pages, a cheaper join. <bookmark mark='c'/> Or, as the optimizer chose, look up whale in an index, fetch only those rows, and join the books to them: eighty-five pages instead of twelve hundred. Its guess was off, ten whale rows where there are eighty-one, but the choice was still right. Chapter 7 shows what happens when a guess is far worse.
72e3c9f8a1aa.zh: 第一个选择是怎样到达每张表：全部读一遍，还是用索引。这是在语料样本上的 whale 查询，有三种做法。<bookmark mark='a'/>扫描词表，用嵌套循环连接。<bookmark mark='b'/>扫描再做哈希连接：页数一样，连接更便宜。<bookmark mark='c'/>或者，像优化器选择的那样，在索引里查 whale，只取出那些行，再把书连接上去：八十五页，而不是一千二百页。它的猜测偏了，以为有十行 whale，实际有八十一行，但选择依然正确。第7章会展示猜测错得多时会发生什么。

7cca64f3a3fe.en: Chapter five. Joins, page by page.
7cca64f3a3fe.zh: 第五章。连接，一页一页地算。

4716e79aae63.en: To compare join algorithms, count what is expensive. <bookmark mark='a'/> A disk moves whole pages, and in Part 34 a random page cost milliseconds while the processor's work on it cost microseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the cost of a join is the number of pages read and written, given the size of each table in pages, M and N, and the number of pages of memory, B. Here R has four hundred pages and S two hundred. <bookmark mark='c'/> The simplest join fills memory with a block of R, keeping two pages for input and output, and reads all of S to find the matches, then the next block, and again. <bookmark mark='d'/> With five pages of memory, that is a hundred and thirty-four blocks, each reading all of S: twenty-seven thousand page reads, to join tables that hold only six hundred.
4716e79aae63.zh: 要比较连接算法，就去数那些昂贵的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>磁盘按整页搬运数据，在第34部分，随机读一页要几毫秒，而处理器处理它只要几微秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以连接的代价是读写的页数，取决于每张表的页数 M 和 N，以及内存的页数 B。这里 R 有四百页，S 有二百页。<bookmark mark='c'/>最简单的连接把 R 的一块装满内存，留两页做输入和输出，然后读遍 S 找匹配，再换下一块，如此反复。<bookmark mark='d'/>内存有五页时，那就是一百三十四块，每块都读遍 S：两万七千次读页，只为连接两张总共才六百页的表。

594b80b3d479.en: There are four classic ways to join. <bookmark mark='a'/> Block nested loops, which needs nothing: no index, no order. <bookmark mark='b'/> Index nested loops: for each row of R, look its key up in an index on S. Each lookup costs a page or two, so it wins when R is small. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sort-merge: sort both tables on the join key, with Part 16's external merge sort, then walk them together once. Its cost is the sorting passes, and its output comes out in order, which a later operator may want. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the hash join, in the form first built for the Grace database machine in Tokyo: hash both tables into buckets on disk, so that matching rows land in matching buckets, then join each pair of buckets in memory. Every page is read, written and read again: three times M plus N, as long as each bucket fits in memory.
594b80b3d479.zh: 经典的连接方法有四种。<bookmark mark='a'/>块嵌套循环，什么都不需要：不要索引，也不要顺序。<bookmark mark='b'/>索引嵌套循环：对 R 的每一行，到 S 上的索引里查它的键。每次查找花一两页，所以当 R 很小时它最好。<bookmark mark='c'/>排序归并：用第16部分的外部归并排序把两张表都按连接键排好，再一起走一遍。它的代价是排序的那几趟，而它的输出是有序的，后面的运算符可能正需要。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有哈希连接，最初是为东京的 Grace 数据库机器构建的形式：把两张表都哈希进磁盘上的桶，使匹配的行落在相应的桶里，再在内存里逐对连接这些桶。每一页被读一次、写一次、再读一次：三倍的 M 加 N，只要每个桶都放得进内存。

671b32a06526.en: Formulas like these fill database textbooks. Our joins count every page they touch, so we can check them, for five sizes of memory. <bookmark mark='a'/> Block nested loops and sort-merge match their formulas exactly, page for page. <bookmark mark='b'/> Index nested loops reads less than its formula, because the formula assumes every probe finds a match, and thirteen percent of R's keys have none. <bookmark mark='c'/> The hash join pays a little for buckets whose last page is half full, and with under forty pages of memory a bucket no longer fits, so a real system would partition it again. <bookmark mark='d'/> Most important, the winner changes. With eighty pages of memory the simplest join is the cheapest; with five, hashing is fifteen times cheaper. The right algorithm depends on the sizes, and only the database knows the sizes. That is why it, and not the programmer, should choose.
671b32a06526.zh: 数据库教科书里满是这样的公式。我们的连接会数下它们碰过的每一页，所以可以在五种内存大小下检验这些公式。<bookmark mark='a'/>块嵌套循环和排序归并与公式完全吻合，一页不差。<bookmark mark='b'/>索引嵌套循环读得比公式少，因为公式假设每次探查都能找到匹配，而 R 的键里有百分之十三一个也找不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>哈希连接为最后一页只装了一半的桶付出一点代价，而内存少于四十页时，一个桶就放不下了，真实系统会把它再分区一次。<bookmark mark='d'/>最重要的是，赢家会变。内存有八十页时，最简单的连接最便宜；只有五页时，哈希便宜十五倍。正确的算法取决于大小，而只有数据库知道大小。这就是为什么该由它，而不是程序员，来选择。

d262ec000d22.en: Here is a query that joins five tables in a chain, a to b to c to d to e, with sizes from fifty rows to thirty thousand, asking for the rows of a with small ids. <bookmark mark='a'/> Joins can be done in any order. Joining one table at a time, five tables can be ordered a hundred and twenty ways; allowing joins of joins, sixteen hundred and eighty. With twelve tables, which real queries reach, there are half a billion orders, and twenty-eight trillion trees. <bookmark mark='b'/> And each join has four algorithms, and each table may have indexes. Nobody can try them all. <bookmark mark='c'/> But look at the last column: the number of subsets of the tables grows far more slowly. That is the key to the solution.
d262ec000d22.zh: 这个查询把五张表连成一条链，a 到 b 到 c 到 d 到 e，大小从五十行到三万行不等，要的是 a 中 id 较小的那些行。<bookmark mark='a'/>连接可以按任何顺序做。一次连一张表，五张表有一百二十种顺序；允许连接的连接，有一千六百八十种。到了十二张表，真实查询会达到这个数，就有五亿种顺序、二十八万亿棵树。<bookmark mark='b'/>而每个连接有四种算法，每张表还可能有索引。没人能全部试一遍。<bookmark mark='c'/>但请看最后一列：表的子集数目增长得慢得多。这就是解法的关键。

7a64b78408f2.en: Does the order matter? We can cost all hundred and twenty left-deep orders of our five tables, using hash joins throughout. <bookmark mark='a'/> They all compute the same count. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best starts with the ten rows of a that pass the filter, and grows along the chain, keeping intermediate results small: twenty-three hundred pages. The median order costs twenty times as much. <bookmark mark='c'/> The worst starts with b and d, which no condition connects, so the first join is a cross product, six hundred million pairs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Between the best and the worst is a factor of ten thousand. Choosing the order is the optimizer's most important decision.
7a64b78408f2.zh: 顺序要紧吗？我们可以给五张表的全部一百二十种左深顺序算出代价，全都用哈希连接。<bookmark mark='a'/>它们算出的计数都一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>最好的顺序从 a 中通过过滤的十行开始，沿着链往下长，让中间结果保持很小：两千三百页。中位数的顺序要贵二十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>最差的顺序从 b 和 d 开始，而没有任何条件连接它们，所以第一个连接是笛卡儿积，六亿对。<bookmark mark='d'/>最好与最差之间相差一万倍。选择顺序是优化器最重要的决定。

b6cf16f81850.en: Patricia Selinger's team at IBM found the method in 1979, for System R, and nearly every optimizer since descends from it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Work up from small sets of tables to large. For each set, keep only the cheapest plan that joins exactly those tables. <bookmark mark='b'/> To plan a set of tables, take away one table, look up the best plan for the rest, which is already known, and join the table back on, with every algorithm; keep the best result. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is dynamic programming, from Part 19, and it works because the best plan for a set is built from the best plans for its parts. <bookmark mark='d'/> One refinement: a more expensive sub-plan may be worth keeping if its output is sorted, because a later merge join or ORDER BY gets the order for free. Selinger called these interesting orders. <bookmark mark='e'/> Our database's optimizer does this. It costed 395 plans, where trying every order and algorithm costs twelve hundred, and found the same plan: start with a's ten rows, join along the chain. With more tables the gap becomes astronomical.
b6cf16f81850.zh: IBM 的 Patricia Selinger 团队在 1979 年为 System R 找到了方法，此后几乎每个优化器都源于它。<bookmark mark='a'/>从小的表集合往大的做。对每个集合，只保留恰好连接这些表的最便宜的计划。<bookmark mark='b'/>要为一组表做计划，就拿掉一张表，查出其余表的最佳计划，那已经知道了，再用每种算法把这张表连回去；保留最好的结果。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是第19部分的动态规划，它之所以成立，是因为一个集合的最佳计划由其各部分的最佳计划构成。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有一处改进：一个更贵的子计划如果输出是有序的，也许值得保留，因为后面的归并连接或 ORDER BY 能免费得到顺序。Selinger 称之为有趣的顺序。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们数据库的优化器就是这样做的。它给 395 个计划算了代价，而尝试每种顺序和算法要一千二百个，并找到了同一个计划：从 a 的十行开始，沿着链连接下去。表再多一些，差距就变得天文数字般巨大。

2b8545eb1601.en: The optimizer's costs depend on how many rows each step produces, and it cannot know that without running the query. It guesses, from statistics. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our database keeps, for each table, the number of rows, and for each column the number of distinct values and the smallest and largest. <bookmark mark='b'/> An equality condition is guessed to keep one row in the number of distinct values; a range, the fraction of the span it covers. <bookmark mark='c'/> And two conditions together are assumed independent, so their fractions multiply. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here are a hundred thousand people. One city: the guess is five hundred, the truth 492. An age range: almost exact. A city and an age, which really are independent: right again. <bookmark mark='e'/> But a city and its own country: the guess is twenty-five, the truth 492. The country adds nothing once the city is known, and the independence assumption cannot see that.
2b8545eb1601.zh: 优化器的代价取决于每一步产出多少行，而不运行查询，它无从得知。它只能根据统计信息去猜。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的数据库为每张表记下行数，为每一列记下不同值的个数，以及最小值和最大值。<bookmark mark='b'/>等值条件被猜测为保留不同值个数分之一的行；范围条件，则是它覆盖的区间所占的比例。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个条件同时出现时，假定它们相互独立，于是比例相乘。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里有十万个人。一个城市：猜测是五百，真值 492。一个年龄范围：几乎精确。一个城市加一个年龄，两者确实独立：又对了。<bookmark mark='e'/>但一个城市加它自己所在的国家：猜测是二十五，真值 492。一旦知道了城市，国家就不再提供任何信息，而独立性假设看不出这一点。

8a89ea0539f2.en: Distinct counts assume every value is equally common, and real data is rarely like that. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a sample of the novels, a hundred and twenty thousand words with twelve thousand distinct, the guess for any single word is ten rows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Whale, eighty-one. Ship, twenty-six. Zeal, none at all. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the: six thousand, seven hundred and seventy-six. Word frequencies follow Zipf's law, which we met in Part 17, and the guess is wrong by a factor of almost seven hundred. <bookmark mark='d'/> A plan chosen for ten rows, a nested loop with an index probe per row, is a disaster for seven thousand. <bookmark mark='e'/> So real systems keep histograms, and a list of each column's most common values with their counts.
8a89ea0539f2.zh: 不同值的个数隐含着每个值同样常见的假设，而真实数据很少是这样。<bookmark mark='a'/>在小说的一个样本里，有十二万个词，其中一万二千个不同，对任何一个词的猜测都是十行。<bookmark mark='b'/>whale，八十一。ship，二十六。zeal，一个也没有。<bookmark mark='c'/>而 the：六千七百七十六。词频服从齐普夫定律，我们在第17部分见过，于是这个猜测错了将近七百倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个为十行选定的计划，每行做一次索引探查的嵌套循环，碰上七千行就是一场灾难。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以真实系统会保留直方图，以及每一列最常见值的列表和它们的计数。

26be3665a83f.en: In a query with several joins, the errors compound. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each join's output is estimated from the estimates of its inputs, times a guessed fraction, so the errors multiply. Our chain query's guesses drift: four hundred rows guessed where 376 came, then 343, and by the end, thirty-nine thousand guessed for twenty thousand. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ioannidis and Christodoulakis proved in 1991 that such errors can grow exponentially with the number of joins. <bookmark mark='c'/> And when Viktor Leis and colleagues tested real optimizers on real data in 2015, they found estimates wrong by factors of ten thousand and more in every system. <bookmark mark='d'/> What saves us is that a plan only has to be good, not perfect, and a factor of two rarely changes the choice. <bookmark mark='e'/> When it does, systems now re-optimize in the middle of a query, or sample the data, or learn the estimates from experience, which is where the frontier is.
26be3665a83f.zh: 在一个有多个连接的查询里，误差会叠加。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个连接的输出，都是由它输入的估计值乘上一个猜测的比例得来的，所以误差相乘。我们的链式查询的猜测一路漂移：猜四百行，来了 376 行，然后是 343 行，到最后，猜三万九千行，实际两万行。<bookmark mark='b'/>Ioannidis 和 Christodoulakis 在 1991 年证明，这样的误差可以随连接数目呈指数增长。<bookmark mark='c'/>而当 Viktor Leis 和同事在 2015 年用真实数据测试真实的优化器时，他们在每一个系统里都发现了错一万倍乃至更多的估计。<bookmark mark='d'/>救了我们的是：计划只需要好，不需要完美，而两倍的误差很少改变选择。<bookmark mark='e'/>当它确实改变选择时，如今的系统会在查询中途重新优化，或者对数据抽样，或者从经验中学习估计，那正是前沿所在。

98107c0bf9ce.en: The index nearly every database uses is the B-tree of Rudolf Bayer and Edward McCreight, from 1972, in the variant called the B-plus tree. Here we insert twelve words from Moby Dick into a tiny one, where each node holds at most three keys. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first three go into one leaf, in order. <bookmark mark='b'/> The fourth overflows it. The leaf splits into two, and a copy of the first key of the right half goes up into a new root, as a separator: smaller keys to the left, others to the right. <bookmark mark='c'/> More inserts, more leaf splits, and each split adds a separator to the root. <bookmark mark='d'/> When the root itself is full, it splits, and a new root appears above it. That is the only way the tree grows taller, so every leaf is always at the same depth, and the tree is always balanced. <bookmark mark='e'/> To search, start at the root and follow the separators down, one node per level. <bookmark mark='f'/> And all the keys are in the leaves, linked in order, so a range is a search for its first key followed by a walk along the leaves.
98107c0bf9ce.zh: 几乎每个数据库都在用的索引，是 Rudolf Bayer 和 Edward McCreight 在 1972 年提出的 B 树，用的是称为 B+ 树的变体。这里我们把《白鲸》里的十二个词插入一棵很小的树，每个节点最多放三个键。<bookmark mark='a'/>前三个按顺序进了一个叶子。<bookmark mark='b'/>第四个让它溢出。叶子一分为二，右半部分第一个键的一份拷贝升到一个新的根里，作为分隔符：小的键在左，其余在右。<bookmark mark='c'/>插入更多，叶子分裂更多，每次分裂都给根添一个分隔符。<bookmark mark='d'/>当根本身满了，它也分裂，上面出现一个新的根。这是树长高的唯一方式，所以每个叶子总在同一深度，树总是平衡的。<bookmark mark='e'/>查找时，从根开始，顺着分隔符往下走，每层一个节点。<bookmark mark='f'/>而所有的键都在叶子里，按顺序链接，所以范围查询就是找到它的第一个键，再沿着叶子走下去。

86ef6d4f3adf.en: In a real database each node is a page of the disk. <bookmark mark='a'/> A four-kilobyte page holds about four hundred keys and pointers, so each level multiplies the number of keys reachable by four hundred. <bookmark mark='b'/> A thousand keys need two levels, a million three, a billion four, a trillion five. The top levels are small enough to stay in memory, so finding any key costs about one read from the disk. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our database's index on the Job's word column covers four point six million rows and fifty-eight thousand distinct words in a tree two levels high. <bookmark mark='d'/> A binary search tree, from Part 17, would be at least sixteen levels deep, and on a disk each level is a seek. <bookmark mark='e'/> The price is paid on writes: each insert may split nodes, and a table with five indexes does six writes for every new row.
86ef6d4f3adf.zh: 在真实的数据库里，每个节点是磁盘上的一页。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个四千字节的页大约能放四百个键和指针，所以每一层都让可达的键数乘以四百。<bookmark mark='b'/>一千个键需要两层，一百万个三层，十亿个四层，一万亿个五层。顶上几层小到可以一直留在内存里，所以找任何一个键大约只要读一次磁盘。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们数据库在任务的词列上建的索引，覆盖四百六十万行、五万八千个不同的词，树只有两层高。<bookmark mark='d'/>第17部分的二叉搜索树至少要十六层深，而在磁盘上，每一层就是一次寻道。<bookmark mark='e'/>代价在写入时付出：每次插入都可能让节点分裂，而一张有五个索引的表，每插入一行就要写六次。

189c281c5443.en: Finding keys in the index is only half of the work: the rows themselves must be fetched. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the range from whale to whales: seventeen hundred rows of the Job's four point six million. <bookmark mark='b'/> The words table is stored in the order of the books, so those rows are scattered, and fetching them touches 966 different pages, more than one for every two rows. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the table were stored sorted by word, clustered on that key, the same rows would sit together on eighteen pages, fifty times fewer. <bookmark mark='d'/> A table can be in only one order, so it can be clustered on only one key, and the optimizer accounts for this when it estimates the cost of using an index. <bookmark mark='e'/> There are other kinds of index for other jobs: hash indexes for pure equality, bitmaps for analytics, the LSM trees of Part 34 for heavy writing, and inverted indexes for text. <bookmark mark='f'/> And an index that contains every column a query needs answers it without reading the table at all.
189c281c5443.zh: 在索引里找到键只是一半的工作：行本身还得取出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>看从 whale 到 whales 的范围：任务的四百六十万行中的一千七百行。<bookmark mark='b'/>词表是按书的顺序存放的，所以这些行是分散的，取出它们要碰 966 个不同的页，每两行就超过一页。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果表按词排序存放，也就是在这个键上聚簇，同样的行会挤在十八页上，少了五十倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>一张表只能有一种顺序，所以只能在一个键上聚簇，而优化器在估计使用索引的代价时会把这一点算进去。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有别的索引做别的事：哈希索引只管等值，位图索引用于分析，第34部分的 LSM 树用于大量写入，倒排索引用于文本。<bookmark mark='f'/>而一个包含查询所需全部列的索引，回答查询时根本不用读表。

5a4eb9d355a6.en: Now the second machine inside a database. Move a hundred from Ana's account to Ben's: two updates, wrapped in a transaction. <bookmark mark='a'/> It must be atomic: if the machine crashes between the updates, the money must not vanish from one account without arriving in the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each transaction, run alone, keeps the data consistent: here, the total stays the same. <bookmark mark='c'/> It must be isolated: while thousands of transactions run at once, each must behave as if it ran by itself. <bookmark mark='d'/> And it must be durable: once the commit returns, the transfer survives any crash. <bookmark mark='e'/> Jim Gray set out these ideas; Härder and Reuter gave them their initials, ACID. Atomicity and durability come in chapter thirteen. Isolation takes the next four.
5a4eb9d355a6.zh: 现在来看数据库里的第二台机器。从 Ana 的账户转一百给 Ben：两次更新，包在一个事务里。<bookmark mark='a'/>它必须是原子的：如果机器在两次更新之间崩溃，钱不能从一个账户消失却没有到达另一个。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个事务单独运行时，都保持数据的一致：这里，总额不变。<bookmark mark='c'/>它必须是隔离的：成千上万的事务同时运行时，每一个都必须表现得像是独自运行。<bookmark mark='d'/>它还必须是持久的：一旦提交返回，这笔转账就能挺过任何崩溃。<bookmark mark='e'/>Jim Gray 阐明了这些想法；Härder 和 Reuter 用首字母给它们起名为 ACID。原子性和持久性在第十三章讲。隔离性占接下来的四章。

ff16f7db06e0.en: What does it mean for interleaved transactions to be correct? A schedule is the order in which their steps happen. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here two transactions each read x and write it back, plus something: two deposits. Both read the old balance; both write; the second write overwrites the first, and one deposit is lost. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two steps conflict if they come from different transactions, touch the same item, and at least one writes; then their order matters. Draw an arrow from the transaction that went first to the one that went second. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here T1 read x before T2 wrote it, and T2 read x before T1 wrote it: arrows both ways, a cycle. No serial order is equivalent. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is another interleaving, of two transactions touching x and y. Every conflict has T1 first, so the graph is one arrow, and the schedule is equivalent to running T1, then T2. <bookmark mark='e'/> That is the theorem of Eswaran, Gray, Lorie and Traiger, from 1976: a schedule is conflict-serializable exactly when its graph has no cycle.
ff16f7db06e0.zh: 交错执行的事务，怎样才算正确？调度就是它们各步发生的顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里两个事务各自读 x，再写回去，加上一点：两笔存款。两者都读到旧余额；两者都写；第二次写覆盖了第一次，一笔存款丢了。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果两步来自不同的事务、涉及同一项、且至少有一步是写，它们就冲突；这时它们的顺序就要紧了。从先发生的那个事务画一条箭头指向后发生的那个。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里 T1 在 T2 写 x 之前读了 x，T2 又在 T1 写 x 之前读了 x：箭头双向，构成一个环。没有任何串行顺序与它等价。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是另一种交错，两个事务涉及 x 和 y。每个冲突都是 T1 在先，所以图只有一条箭头，这个调度等价于先运行 T1，再运行 T2。<bookmark mark='e'/>这就是 Eswaran、Gray、Lorie 和 Traiger 在 1976 年的定理：一个调度是冲突可串行化的，当且仅当它的图没有环。

c73a88f7b419.en: There is a wider definition. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this schedule, T2 and T3 write x without reading it, blind writes, and the conflict graph has a cycle. <bookmark mark='b'/> Yet T1 reads the value it would read if the three ran in order, and the last write is T3's, as in that order. The schedule is view serializable: no one could tell the difference. <bookmark mark='c'/> But testing view serializability is NP-complete, as Christos Papadimitriou showed in 1979, while a cycle check takes linear time. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our checker enumerates all ninety interleavings of three small transactions. Ten are conflict-serializable, and here no others are view-serializable either. <bookmark mark='e'/> So databases aim for conflict serializability, and they must achieve it on the fly, deciding each step as it arrives, without knowing what comes next.
c73a88f7b419.zh: 还有一个更宽的定义。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这个调度里，T2 和 T3 不读就写 x，叫盲写，冲突图有一个环。<bookmark mark='b'/>可 T1 读到的值，正是三者按顺序运行时它会读到的，最后一次写是 T3 的，也与那个顺序一致。这个调度是视图可串行化的：没有人能分辨出差别。<bookmark mark='c'/>但检验视图可串行化是 NP 完全的，Christos Papadimitriou 在 1979 年证明了这一点，而检查环只要线性时间。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的检查器枚举了三个小事务的全部九十种交错。其中十种是冲突可串行化的，而这里也没有别的视图可串行化的。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以数据库以冲突可串行化为目标，而且必须在运行中实现它，每一步来了就要决定，不知道接下来会发生什么。

3d2fa03832f5.en: The classic answer is locking. <bookmark mark='a'/> Before reading an item, a transaction takes a shared lock on it; before writing, an exclusive lock. Many readers can share, but a writer excludes everyone, and a request that conflicts must wait. <bookmark mark='b'/> Locks alone are not enough. The rule that makes them work is two-phase locking: a transaction may acquire locks, then release them, but never acquire another after its first release. Its locks grow, peak, and shrink. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here is why this suffices. If T i comes before T j in the conflict graph, then T j obtained a lock that T i had released, so T i passed its peak, its lock point, first. <bookmark mark='d'/> A cycle in the graph would put some lock point before itself, which is impossible. So every schedule two-phase locking allows is serializable, equivalent to running the transactions in the order of their lock points. <bookmark mark='e'/> In practice the locks are held until commit, strict two-phase locking, so that nobody reads a value that might still be rolled back. <bookmark mark='f'/> And there are choices about what to lock, rows or pages or whole tables, and how to lock ranges, so that a new row cannot appear in the middle of someone's query.
3d2fa03832f5.zh: 经典的答案是锁。<bookmark mark='a'/>读一项之前，事务对它加共享锁；写之前，加排他锁。许多读者可以共享，但一个写者排斥所有人，冲突的请求必须等待。<bookmark mark='b'/>光有锁还不够。让锁起作用的规则是两阶段锁：事务可以先获得锁，再释放锁，但第一次释放之后就再也不能获得新锁。它持有的锁先增长，到达顶峰，再收缩。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是它足够的原因。如果在冲突图里 T i 排在 T j 之前，那么 T j 拿到了一把 T i 释放的锁，所以 T i 先过了它的顶峰，也就是它的锁点。<bookmark mark='d'/>图里的一个环会让某个锁点排在它自己之前，这不可能。所以两阶段锁允许的每个调度都是可串行化的，等价于按锁点的顺序运行这些事务。<bookmark mark='e'/>实践中锁一直持有到提交，即严格两阶段锁，这样就没人会读到一个可能还会被回滚的值。<bookmark mark='f'/>还要选择锁什么，行、页还是整张表，以及怎样锁住范围，使得新的一行不能出现在别人查询的中途。

b1ce9c60b1ad.en: Locking has a price. <bookmark mark='a'/> T1 reads A and will write B; T2 reads B and will write A. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run them interleaved. Each takes its shared lock. Then T1 asks for B, which T2 holds, and waits; T2 asks for A, which T1 holds, and waits. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each waits for the other, and will wait forever: a deadlock, the cycle in the waits-for graph that Part 33 met in the dining philosophers. <bookmark mark='d'/> A database does not prevent it by careful lock order, because transactions are written by users. It finds the cycle and aborts one transaction, which releases its locks. Our scheduler aborted T2, and T1 finished. T2 can simply be run again.
b1ce9c60b1ad.zh: 锁是有代价的。<bookmark mark='a'/>T1 读 A，将写 B；T2 读 B，将写 A。<bookmark mark='b'/>让它们交错运行。各自拿到共享锁。然后 T1 要 B，B 在 T2 手里，于是等待；T2 要 A，A 在 T1 手里，于是也等待。<bookmark mark='c'/>彼此等待对方，将永远等下去：这是死锁，就是第33部分在哲学家就餐问题里遇到的等待图中的环。<bookmark mark='d'/>数据库不靠小心安排加锁顺序来防止它，因为事务是用户写的。它找出环，中止一个事务，让它释放锁。我们的调度器中止了 T2，T1 完成了。T2 只需重新运行一次。

ca1d24fb447f.en: There are two families of remedy. <bookmark mark='a'/> Detection lets transactions wait, and looks for cycles. <bookmark mark='b'/> Prevention uses age. In wait-die, an older transaction may wait for a younger one, but a younger one that asks for an older one's lock is aborted on the spot. <bookmark mark='c'/> In wound-wait, it is the other way round: an older transaction aborts the younger holder, and a younger one waits. <bookmark mark='d'/> Either way, waiting only goes in one direction of age, so no cycle can form, and a restarted transaction keeps its original age, so it eventually becomes the oldest and wins. <bookmark mark='e'/> We ran four hundred random mixes of four transactions under each policy. Every resulting schedule passed the serializability check. Detection found 342 deadlocks and aborted only those; the prevention schemes never deadlocked, but aborted more than twice as many transactions, many of which would never have deadlocked. That is why most systems detect.
ca1d24fb447f.zh: 补救办法有两大类。<bookmark mark='a'/>检测：让事务等待，同时寻找环。<bookmark mark='b'/>预防：利用年龄。在等待-死亡中，老事务可以等年轻事务，而年轻事务若去要老事务的锁，就当场被中止。<bookmark mark='c'/>在伤害-等待中，正好反过来：老事务中止持锁的年轻事务，而年轻事务等待。<bookmark mark='d'/>无论哪种，等待都只朝年龄的一个方向，所以不会形成环；而重启的事务保留原来的年龄，所以它终将成为最老的而胜出。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们在每种策略下运行了四百组随机的四事务组合。每个产生的调度都通过了可串行化检查。检测法找到 342 个死锁，只中止了这些；预防法从不死锁，却中止了两倍多的事务，其中许多本来永远不会死锁。这就是大多数系统采用检测的原因。

fe09fd644129.en: Locking is pessimistic: it assumes conflict and makes transactions wait. <bookmark mark='a'/> H. T. Kung and John Robinson proposed the opposite in 1981. Let each transaction run freely on private copies, and check only at the end: did any transaction that committed in the meantime write something I read? If not, install my writes; if so, start again. <bookmark mark='b'/> Nobody waits and nothing deadlocks. When conflicts are rare this is fast; when they are common, work is thrown away again and again. <bookmark mark='c'/> A third method gives each transaction a timestamp when it starts, and rejects any read or write that arrives too late to fit that order. <bookmark mark='d'/> All three produce serializable schedules. They differ in who waits, and who starts over.
fe09fd644129.zh: 锁是悲观的：它假定会有冲突，让事务等待。<bookmark mark='a'/>H. T. Kung 和 John Robinson 在 1981 年提出了相反的做法。让每个事务在私有副本上自由运行，只在最后检查：在此期间提交的事务，有没有写过我读过的东西？没有，就安装我的写；有，就从头再来。<bookmark mark='b'/>没人等待，也没有死锁。冲突少时这很快；冲突多时，工作一遍又一遍地被扔掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三种方法在每个事务开始时给它一个时间戳，拒绝任何来得太晚、无法放进这个顺序的读或写。<bookmark mark='d'/>三种方法都产生可串行化的调度。它们的区别在于谁等待，谁重来。

aec0b685cd3b.en: What most databases actually do today is keep the old versions. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each write creates a new version of the item, stamped with the time its transaction committed, and the old ones remain. <bookmark mark='b'/> A transaction that started at time nine reads the newest version committed before nine, here twenty-five, however many writes have come since. <bookmark mark='c'/> It sees a consistent snapshot of the whole database as of its start. This is multiversion concurrency control, from David Reed's thesis of 1978. <bookmark mark='d'/> Readers never wait for writers, and writers never wait for readers. <bookmark mark='e'/> Only two writers of the same item collide, and the first to commit wins. <bookmark mark='f'/> This is snapshot isolation. It is what Oracle gives when you ask for serializable, and what PostgreSQL gives at repeatable read. It feels serializable. It is not.
aec0b685cd3b.zh: 如今大多数数据库实际的做法，是保留旧版本。<bookmark mark='a'/>每次写都为该项创建一个新版本，盖上它的事务提交的时间，旧版本仍然保留。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个在时刻九开始的事务，读到的是九之前提交的最新版本，这里是二十五，不管此后又有多少次写。<bookmark mark='c'/>它看到的是整个数据库在它开始时的一致快照。这就是多版本并发控制，出自 David Reed 1978 年的博士论文。<bookmark mark='d'/>读者从不等待写者，写者也从不等待读者。<bookmark mark='e'/>只有写同一项的两个写者会相撞，先提交者胜。<bookmark mark='f'/>这就是快照隔离。你向 Oracle 要可串行化时它给的就是这个，PostgreSQL 在可重复读级别给的也是这个。它感觉上是可串行化的。其实不是。

896872cf0e12.en: Here is the classic counterexample. A hospital requires at least one doctor on call. Alice and Bob are both on call, and both feel ill. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each runs the same transaction: count the doctors on call, and if there are two, take myself off. <bookmark mark='b'/> Under snapshot isolation, both start from the same snapshot, both count two, and Alice takes herself off while Bob takes himself off. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our database, run at each isolation level, shows the result. At read committed and at snapshot isolation, both commit, and nobody is on call. <bookmark mark='d'/> The two transactions wrote different rows, so the first-committer rule never fired. Yet in any serial order the second would have counted one and stayed. This anomaly is write skew. At the serializable level, with two-phase locking, one of them is aborted and the rule holds.
896872cf0e12.zh: 这是经典的反例。医院要求至少有一位医生值班。Alice 和 Bob 都在值班，两人都觉得不舒服。<bookmark mark='a'/>每人运行同一个事务：数一数值班的医生，如果有两位，就把自己撤下。<bookmark mark='b'/>在快照隔离下，两人从同一个快照开始，都数到两位，于是 Alice 撤下了自己，Bob 也撤下了自己。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的数据库在每个隔离级别下运行，给出了结果。在读已提交和快照隔离下，两者都提交了，没有人值班。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个事务写的是不同的行，所以先提交者规则从未触发。可在任何串行顺序里，第二个人都会数到一位而留下。这种异常叫写偏斜。在可串行化级别下，用两阶段锁，其中一个被中止，规则得以保持。

7c337be5d3b0.en: Can snapshots be made serializable without giving up their speed? <bookmark mark='a'/> Look at what happened. T1 read Bob's row, which T2 then overwrote: an arrow from T1 to T2, called a read-write antidependency. And T2 read Alice's row, which T1 overwrote: an arrow back. A cycle. <bookmark mark='b'/> Alan Fekete and colleagues proved in 2005 that every anomaly of snapshot isolation contains a transaction with such an arrow coming in and another going out. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2008 Michael Cahill turned this into an algorithm: track the read-write arrows as transactions run, and abort any transaction that becomes such a pivot. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our database implements it. T1 is aborted, Alice stays on call, and readers still never wait. <bookmark mark='e'/> PostgreSQL has used this method for its serializable level since 2011. Its cost is an occasional abort that was not strictly necessary.
7c337be5d3b0.zh: 能不能让快照变得可串行化，而又不放弃它的速度？<bookmark mark='a'/>看看发生了什么。T1 读了 Bob 的行，随后 T2 覆盖了它：一条从 T1 指向 T2 的箭头，叫读写反依赖。T2 读了 Alice 的行，T1 覆盖了它：一条箭头指回来。一个环。<bookmark mark='b'/>Alan Fekete 和同事在 2005 年证明，快照隔离的每一种异常，都包含一个有这样一条箭头进来、另一条出去的事务。<bookmark mark='c'/>2008 年，Michael Cahill 把它变成了一个算法：在事务运行时跟踪读写箭头，任何事务一旦成为这样的枢纽就中止它。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的数据库实现了它。T1 被中止，Alice 继续值班，而读者仍然从不等待。<bookmark mark='e'/>PostgreSQL 自 2011 年起就用这种方法实现它的可串行化级别。代价是偶尔有一次并非严格必要的中止。

02f304c9d2a4.en: SQL lets each transaction choose how much isolation it gets. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our database implements six levels, and we ran each of five classic anomalies against each, as a little program and an interleaving, and recorded whether the anomaly happened. <bookmark mark='b'/> A dirty read sees a write that is later rolled back. A non-repeatable read reads the same item twice and gets two values. A lost update we have seen. A phantom is a row that appears between two counts. Write skew is the doctors. <bookmark mark='c'/> Read uncommitted permits everything. Read committed, the default in PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQL Server, stops only dirty reads. Repeatable read, with locks on what was read, stops all but phantoms. Snapshot isolation stops phantoms but not write skew: the two weaker-than-serializable levels fail in different places, so neither is stronger than the other. <bookmark mark='d'/> And only the serializable levels, by locking or by SSI, stop all five.
02f304c9d2a4.zh: SQL 让每个事务选择自己要多少隔离。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的数据库实现了六个级别，我们把五种经典异常各写成一个小程序和一种交错，在每个级别下运行，记录异常是否发生。<bookmark mark='b'/>脏读看到了一个后来被回滚的写。不可重复读两次读同一项，得到两个值。丢失更新我们见过了。幻读是在两次计数之间冒出来的一行。写偏斜就是那两位医生。<bookmark mark='c'/>读未提交什么都允许。读已提交是 PostgreSQL、Oracle 和 SQL Server 的默认级别，只阻止脏读。可重复读给读过的东西加锁，阻止了幻读以外的一切。快照隔离阻止了幻读，却没阻止写偏斜：两个弱于可串行化的级别在不同的地方失败，所以谁也不比谁强。<bookmark mark='d'/>只有可串行化的级别，无论靠锁还是靠 SSI，阻止了全部五种。

f97210908ecf.en: The standard's definitions turned out to be a problem. <bookmark mark='a'/> SQL-92 defined each level by the phenomena it forbids, described in English. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1995 Hal Berenson, Phil Bernstein, Jim Gray and colleagues showed that the wording was ambiguous, that it missed anomalies such as lost updates and write skew, and that snapshot isolation, already shipping, fitted none of the levels. <bookmark mark='c'/> Atul Adya's thesis of 1999 put it right. Draw a graph whose nodes are committed transactions and whose edges are the dependencies between them: who read whose write, who overwrote whose, who overwrote what someone else had read. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each level forbids a kind of cycle. Serializable forbids them all; snapshot isolation allows a cycle with two consecutive anti-dependencies, which is write skew. <bookmark mark='e'/> These definitions do not mention locks or versions, so they apply to any implementation, and can be checked after the fact on what actually happened. <bookmark mark='f'/> That is exactly what the tool Elle does, and testing real databases with it has found many that do not deliver the level they promise.
f97210908ecf.zh: 标准里的定义后来成了问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>SQL-92 用每个级别所禁止的现象来定义它，用英语描述。<bookmark mark='b'/>1995 年，Hal Berenson、Phil Bernstein、Jim Gray 和同事指出，这些措辞含糊不清，漏掉了丢失更新和写偏斜这样的异常，而且已经在产品里出现的快照隔离，放不进任何一个级别。<bookmark mark='c'/>Atul Adya 1999 年的博士论文纠正了这一点。画一个图，节点是已提交的事务，边是它们之间的依赖：谁读了谁的写，谁覆盖了谁的写，谁覆盖了别人读过的东西。<bookmark mark='d'/>每个级别禁止某一类环。可串行化全部禁止；快照隔离允许含两条连续反依赖的环，也就是写偏斜。<bookmark mark='e'/>这些定义不提锁或版本，所以适用于任何实现，也可以事后在实际发生的历史上检查。<bookmark mark='f'/>这正是 Elle 这个工具所做的，用它测试真实的数据库，发现了许多没有兑现其承诺级别的系统。

060ed1f79f71.en: Part 34 made a file system survive crashes with a journal. A database faces the same problem with stricter demands, and the standard answer is ARIES, by C. Mohan and colleagues at IBM, from 1992. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pages are changed in a buffer in memory, and the buffer writes them back when it likes. ARIES allows it to steal: to write a page that an uncommitted transaction has changed. So after a crash, the disk may hold changes that must be undone. <bookmark mark='b'/> And it allows no-force: a commit does not wait for the data pages to be written. So the disk may lack committed changes, which must be redone. <bookmark mark='c'/> Both are safe because of one rule, write-ahead logging: every change is first described in an append-only log, and a page may go to disk only after its log records have. A transaction has committed when its commit record is on disk. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each log record holds its sequence number, its transaction, the page, the values before and after, and a pointer to the transaction's previous record. And each page records the sequence number of the last change applied to it.
060ed1f79f71.zh: 第34部分用日志让文件系统挺过崩溃。数据库面对同样的问题，要求更严，而标准答案是 ARIES，由 IBM 的 C. Mohan 和同事在 1992 年提出。<bookmark mark='a'/>页在内存的缓冲区里被修改，缓冲区想什么时候写回就什么时候写回。ARIES 允许它窃取：把一个未提交事务改过的页写到磁盘。所以崩溃之后，磁盘上可能有必须撤销的修改。<bookmark mark='b'/>它还允许不强制：提交不等数据页写盘。所以磁盘上可能缺少已提交的修改，必须重做。<bookmark mark='c'/>两者之所以安全，靠的是一条规则，预写日志：每个修改先写进一个只追加的日志，一个页只有在描述它的日志记录写盘之后才能写盘。事务的提交记录写到磁盘上，它就提交了。<bookmark mark='d'/>每条日志记录包含它的序号、所属事务、页、修改前后的值，以及指向该事务上一条记录的指针。每个页则记下最后一个施加于它的修改的序号。

ffe8d7e10026.en: Here is a crash, from our implementation. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three transactions updated four pages. The log that reached the disk has twelve records: T3 made three updates to page 0, committed, and ended; T2 updated page 1 three times and committed; T1 updated pages 3 and 2 and 3 again, and had not committed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the power failed. The buffer pool is gone; the disk has whatever pages happened to be written. <bookmark mark='c'/> Page 0 has the value 72, from T3's first update: its last two updates never reached the disk, though T3 committed. <bookmark mark='d'/> And page 3 holds T1's first change, though T1 never committed. The right state is on the right: every committed change, and none of T1's.
ffe8d7e10026.zh: 这是我们的实现里的一次崩溃。<bookmark mark='a'/>三个事务修改了四个页。到达磁盘的日志有十二条记录：T3 对页 0 做了三次更新，提交并结束；T2 更新页 1 三次并提交；T1 更新了页 3、页 2、又是页 3，还没有提交。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后断电了。缓冲池没了；磁盘上是碰巧写下去的那些页。<bookmark mark='c'/>页 0 的值是 72，来自 T3 的第一次更新：虽然 T3 已经提交，它的后两次更新却从未到达磁盘。<bookmark mark='d'/>而页 3 装着 T1 的第一个修改，尽管 T1 从未提交。正确的状态在最右一列：每个已提交的修改都在，T1 的一个也没有。

870a167ad81a.en: Recovery runs in three passes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Analysis reads the log forward and rebuilds what memory held: which transactions were active, here only T1, the loser, and which pages may have been dirty, which tells redo where to start. <bookmark mark='b'/> Redo reads forward again and repeats history: it reapplies every logged update, including the loser's, except where the page's own sequence number shows the change already reached the disk. Four updates are redone and five skipped. Now the pages are exactly as they were at the instant of the crash. <bookmark mark='c'/> Undo then walks the loser's records backward through their pointers, 11, then 5, then 1, restoring the before values. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each undo is itself logged, as a compensation record, which says where undoing should resume. If the machine crashes during recovery, the next recovery redoes these records and never undoes the same change twice. <bookmark mark='e'/> The result is exactly the committed state.
870a167ad81a.zh: 恢复分三趟进行。<bookmark mark='a'/>分析趟正向读日志，重建内存里原有的东西：哪些事务还活跃，这里只有 T1，即失败者；哪些页可能是脏的，这告诉重做从哪里开始。<bookmark mark='b'/>重做趟再次正向读，重演历史：它重新施加每一个记录下的更新，包括失败者的，除非页自己的序号表明这个修改已经到达磁盘。四个更新被重做，五个被跳过。现在各页恰好回到崩溃那一刻的样子。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后撤销趟顺着指针反向走过失败者的记录，11，然后 5，然后 1，恢复修改前的值。<bookmark mark='d'/>每次撤销本身也记进日志，作为一条补偿记录，说明撤销应当从哪里继续。如果机器在恢复中崩溃，下一次恢复会重做这些记录，而绝不会把同一个修改撤销两次。<bookmark mark='e'/>结果恰好是已提交的状态。

557293ed3b6f.en: One example proves little, so we crash it on purpose. <bookmark mark='a'/> Five hundred random workloads, each cut off by a crash at a random moment, then recovered: every one ends in exactly the committed state. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the same five hundred, crashed again partway through undo, and recovered a second time: all five hundred correct. <bookmark mark='c'/> In real systems, checkpoints bound the work: from time to time the tables that analysis rebuilds are written to the log, and analysis begins there instead of at the start of time. <bookmark mark='d'/> ARIES's ideas, write-ahead logging, repeating history, logged undo, are in DB2 and SQL Server and many others. PostgreSQL gets by with redo alone, because its old row versions stay in the table, and a version written by a transaction that never committed is simply invisible.
557293ed3b6f.zh: 一个例子说明不了多少，所以我们故意让它崩溃。<bookmark mark='a'/>五百个随机工作负载，每个都在随机时刻被一次崩溃打断，然后恢复：每一个都恰好回到已提交的状态。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后同样的五百个，在撤销进行到一半时再次崩溃，第二次恢复：五百个全部正确。<bookmark mark='c'/>在真实系统里，检查点限定了工作量：分析趟要重建的那些表会不时写进日志，分析从那里开始，而不必从时间的起点开始。<bookmark mark='d'/>ARIES 的思想，预写日志、重演历史、记入日志的撤销，存在于 DB2、SQL Server 和许多其他系统中。PostgreSQL 只靠重做就够了，因为它的旧行版本留在表里，而一个从未提交的事务写下的版本，干脆就是不可见的。

49df3cdbb397.en: Everything so far has stored a table row by row, every attribute of a row together on a page. <bookmark mark='a'/> That suits transactions, which fetch or change a whole row: one order, one account. <bookmark mark='b'/> But turn the table sideways and store each column on its own pages. <bookmark mark='c'/> An analytic query, adding up one column over the rows that pass a test on another, touches two attributes of millions of rows. <bookmark mark='d'/> A row store must carry all sixteen columns through the memory hierarchy to get at two. <bookmark mark='e'/> A column store reads only those two, each a contiguous array: an eighth of the bytes.
49df3cdbb397.zh: 到目前为止，表都是一行一行存的，一行的所有属性放在同一页上。<bookmark mark='a'/>这适合事务，事务取出或修改整行：一个订单，一个账户。<bookmark mark='b'/>但把表侧过来，把每一列存在它自己的页上。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个分析查询，对通过另一列检验的行把某一列加起来，要碰的是几百万行的两个属性。<bookmark mark='d'/>行存储为了拿到两列，必须把全部十六列都搬过整个存储层次。<bookmark mark='e'/>列存储只读那两列，每列是一个连续的数组：八分之一的字节。

62e019301cc7.en: We measured this, on a million rows of sixteen columns: add one column where another is under a hundred. <bookmark mark='a'/> Processing one tuple at a time, as an interpreter running the iterator model does, takes seventy-four milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Processing whole arrays of values per operation, which is called vectorized execution, on the row layout: fourteen milliseconds, because the loops are tight and the per-call overhead is paid once per thousand values, not once per row. <bookmark mark='c'/> And vectorized on the column layout: four milliseconds, because it moves sixteen megabytes instead of a hundred and twenty-eight. <bookmark mark='d'/> The other modern answer is to compile each query into machine code, as HyPer does: the compiler of Part 13, invoked for every query.
62e019301cc7.zh: 我们测量了这一点，在一百万行、十六列上：对另一列小于一百的行，把某一列加起来。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次处理一个元组，就像解释器运行迭代器模型那样，要七十四毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次操作处理整个数组的值，这叫向量化执行，在行布局上：十四毫秒，因为循环紧凑，每次调用的开销每一千个值才付一次，而不是每行一次。<bookmark mark='c'/>在列布局上向量化：四毫秒，因为它搬的是十六兆字节，而不是一百二十八兆。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一个现代答案是把每个查询编译成机器码，像 HyPer 那样：第13部分的编译器，为每个查询调用一次。

34cca1236e21.en: Storing columns apart has a second payoff. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Job's words table records, for each word, which book it came from, and the rows are in book order, so that column is thirty long runs. Stored run by run, four point six million values, thirty-seven megabytes, become four hundred and eighty bytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> The word column has fifty-eight thousand distinct values, so each can be replaced by a sixteen-bit code into a dictionary, and twenty-four megabytes become under ten. <bookmark mark='c'/> A column holds values of one type, often sorted, often repeated, and so it has far less entropy than a row of mixed fields. <bookmark mark='d'/> Better still, operators can work on the compressed form directly: the sum of a run is its value times its length. <bookmark mark='e'/> Michael Stonebraker's C-Store showed all of this in 2005. Today almost every analytic system stores columns: Parquet files, BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse, and DuckDB, which runs inside a program the way sqlite does.
34cca1236e21.zh: 把列分开存，还有第二个好处。<bookmark mark='a'/>任务的词表为每个词记下它来自哪本书，而行是按书的顺序排的，所以这一列是三十段长长的连续值。按段存储，四百六十万个值、三十七兆字节，变成了四百八十字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>词这一列有五万八千个不同值，所以每个都可以换成指向字典的十六位编码，二十四兆字节变成不到十兆。<bookmark mark='c'/>一列装的是同一种类型的值，常常有序，常常重复，所以它的熵远低于一行混杂的字段。<bookmark mark='d'/>更好的是，运算符可以直接在压缩形式上工作：一段的和就是它的值乘以它的长度。<bookmark mark='e'/>Michael Stonebraker 的 C-Store 在 2005 年展示了这一切。如今几乎每个分析系统都按列存储：Parquet 文件、BigQuery、Snowflake、ClickHouse，还有 DuckDB，它像 sqlite 一样在程序内部运行。

a6c5e186eb32.en: Chapter fifteen. Our database runs the Job.
a6c5e186eb32.zh: 第十五章。我们的数据库运行任务。

9c52bb07ba96.en: Back to the Job. Our database considered two ways to group the words. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hash aggregation: keep a hash table of counts, one entry per distinct word. Fifty-eight thousand entries fit in memory, so it reads the table once: forty-six thousand pages. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sort aggregation: sort all four point six million rows by word, so equal words are adjacent, and count the runs. The rows do not fit in memory, so the sort writes runs to disk and merges them: five times the page traffic. <bookmark mark='c'/> So it chose hashing. Part 16 sorted the words and Part 17 replaced the sort with a hash table and was six times faster. The optimizer made the same decision from its cost model, without being told.
9c52bb07ba96.zh: 回到任务。我们的数据库考虑了两种给词分组的方法。<bookmark mark='a'/>哈希聚合：维护一个计数的哈希表，每个不同的词一项。五万八千项放得进内存，所以表只读一遍：四万六千页。<bookmark mark='b'/>排序聚合：把全部四百六十万行按词排序，让相同的词相邻，再数出每段。这些行放不进内存，所以排序要把有序段写到磁盘再归并：五倍的页流量。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以它选了哈希。第16部分给词排了序，第17部分用哈希表取代了排序，快了六倍。优化器根据它的代价模型作出了同样的决定，没有人告诉它。

927f093d561c.en: We check our database against sqlite, the most widely deployed database in the world, which ships inside every phone and every browser. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its plan: scan the words, and group them in a temporary B-tree, a sort by another name. <bookmark mark='b'/> Our engine, written in Python, takes seven seconds. Sqlite, in C, takes two and a quarter. <bookmark mark='c'/> Give sqlite an index on the word column and it changes plan by itself: the index holds the words already in order, so it reads the index alone, counting runs, in a quarter of a second. The query did not change. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every one of these gives the same twenty words with the same counts as Part 17's hand-written program.
927f093d561c.zh: 我们拿 sqlite 来核对我们的数据库，它是世界上部署最广的数据库，装在每一部手机和每一个浏览器里。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的计划：扫描词表，在一棵临时 B 树里分组，换个名字的排序。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们的引擎用 Python 写，要七秒。sqlite 用 C 写，要两秒多一点。<bookmark mark='c'/>给 sqlite 在词列上建一个索引，它就自己换了计划：索引里的词已经有序，所以它只读索引，数出每段，四分之一秒。查询没有改动。<bookmark mark='d'/>它们每一个都给出与第17部分手写程序相同的二十个词和相同的计数。

85d67e3ed45b.en: The ledger gets row thirteen. <bookmark mark='a'/> One line of SQL, answered by sqlite on this machine in two and a quarter seconds, and we never said how. <bookmark mark='b'/> That is slower than Part 24's engineered C, by about thirty times, and that program took a whole part to write. <bookmark mark='c'/> With an index it is a quarter of a second. And the same database answers the whale question, or any other, with one more line and no new program. That trade, some speed for never having to say how, is Codd's bargain, and the world took it.
85d67e3ed45b.zh: 账本添上第十三行。<bookmark mark='a'/>一行 SQL，由 sqlite 在这台机器上两秒多一点答完，而我们从没说过怎么做。<bookmark mark='b'/>这比第24部分精心打造的 C 程序慢大约三十倍，而那个程序花了整整一个部分来写。<bookmark mark='c'/>有了索引，是四分之一秒。而且同一个数据库回答 whale 的问题，或者任何别的问题，只要再写一行，不用写新程序。用一些速度换来永远不必说怎么做，这就是 Codd 的交易，而世界接受了它。

268ab8e94f84.en: Not every store is relational. <bookmark mark='a'/> Key-value stores, like Amazon's Dynamo, give up queries for scale: get and put by key, and nothing else. <bookmark mark='b'/> Document stores keep nested records. <bookmark mark='c'/> Graph databases query by path. <bookmark mark='d'/> And distributed SQL systems, like Google's Spanner, keep transactions across many machines, which Part 39 explains. <bookmark mark='e'/> Each new kind began by dropping Codd's model for speed or scale, and most have since added SQL and transactions back. Michael Stonebraker and Andy Pavlo reviewed fifty years of this in 2024, and their title says it: what goes around comes around.
268ab8e94f84.zh: 并不是每种存储都是关系型的。<bookmark mark='a'/>键值存储，比如亚马逊的 Dynamo，为了规模放弃了查询：按键取和放，别的什么都没有。<bookmark mark='b'/>文档存储保存嵌套的记录。<bookmark mark='c'/>图数据库按路径查询。<bookmark mark='d'/>而分布式 SQL 系统，比如谷歌的 Spanner，让事务跨越许多机器，第39部分会讲到。<bookmark mark='e'/>每一种新类型都是从为了速度或规模而抛开 Codd 的模型开始的，而其中大多数后来又把 SQL 和事务加了回去。Michael Stonebraker 和 Andy Pavlo 在 2024 年回顾了这五十年，他们的标题说明了一切：转了一圈，又回来了。

ec3aa3e43d65.en: Chapter sixteen. Frontier: joins, guesses, and guarantees.
ec3aa3e43d65.zh: 第十六章。前沿：连接、猜测与保证。

bb1a1270f1c2.en: Everything in this part's optimizer joins two tables at a time. Here is a query where that is provably the wrong idea. <bookmark mark='a'/> Join an edge table to itself three times to find triangles in a graph: a and b connected, b and c, and c back to a. <bookmark mark='b'/> Any plan made of two-way joins must first join two of the three, which produces every path of two edges. In a graph with a few hubs, a node with d edges makes about d squared over two such paths, and almost none of them close a triangle. <bookmark mark='c'/> On our graphs, four and a half thousand edges give over a million paths, to find four hundred and thirty-two triangles. <bookmark mark='d'/> A different kind of join binds one variable at a time: for each edge, intersect the neighbour lists of its two ends. Ten thousand steps instead of a million.
bb1a1270f1c2.zh: 这一部分的优化器，每次都只连接两张表。这里有一个查询，可以证明这种想法是错的。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一张边表与它自己连接三次，找出图中的三角形：a 与 b 相连，b 与 c 相连，c 又连回 a。<bookmark mark='b'/>任何由两两连接构成的计划，都必须先连接三者中的两个，而这会产出所有长度为二的路径。在有几个枢纽的图里，一个有 d 条边的节点会产生大约 d 的平方除以二条这样的路径，而几乎没有一条能闭合成三角形。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们的图上，四千五百条边产生了一百多万条路径，只为找到四百三十二个三角形。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一种连接一次绑定一个变量：对每条边，求它两端邻居列表的交集。一万步，而不是一百万步。

6370babad4f3.en: How large can the answer to a join be? <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2008 Albert Atserias, Martin Grohe and Dániel Marx gave an exact answer for any join query: the product of the table sizes, each raised to a weight from a small linear program, the fractional edge cover. <bookmark mark='b'/> For triangles, each table gets weight one half, and the bound is N to the three halves: with forty-five hundred edges, at most three hundred thousand triangles could exist. <bookmark mark='c'/> But a plan of binary joins can take time proportional to N squared on such inputs, more than the largest possible answer. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2012 Hung Ngo and colleagues found join algorithms whose running time never exceeds the bound, and Todd Veldhuizen's leapfrog triejoin is a practical one. They are called worst-case optimal. <bookmark mark='e'/> They now appear in commercial and research systems, and the open questions are when to use them instead of ordinary joins, and how to estimate their cost.
6370babad4f3.zh: 连接的答案最多能有多大？<bookmark mark='a'/>2008 年，Albert Atserias、Martin Grohe 和 Dániel Marx 对任何连接查询都给出了确切的答案：各表大小的乘积，每个的指数是一个小线性规划给出的权重，即分数边覆盖。<bookmark mark='b'/>对三角形，每张表的权重是二分之一，上界是 N 的二分之三次方：四千五百条边，最多只能有三十万个三角形。<bookmark mark='c'/>但一个由二元连接构成的计划，在这样的输入上可能花正比于 N 平方的时间，比最大可能的答案还多。<bookmark mark='d'/>2012 年，Hung Ngo 和同事找到了运行时间从不超过这个上界的连接算法，而 Todd Veldhuizen 的跳蛙字典树连接是其中实用的一种。它们被称为最坏情况最优连接。<bookmark mark='e'/>它们现在出现在商业和研究系统中，开放的问题是何时该用它们代替普通连接，以及怎样估计它们的代价。

d2755fe379b5.en: The second frontier is estimation. <bookmark mark='a'/> We saw how badly independence assumptions fail. <bookmark mark='b'/> One line of research trains models, on the data itself or on the queries already run, to predict the sizes of results, capturing correlations that histograms miss. <bookmark mark='c'/> Another learns the plans directly. Neo, in 2019, replaced the optimizer with a neural network trained on experience. Bao, two years later, was more modest: it keeps the classical optimizer and learns only which hints to give it, query by query. <bookmark mark='d'/> The difficulty is trust. A model can be wrong in ways no one predicted, and a query that suddenly takes an hour instead of a second is worse for its users than one that was always a little slow. <bookmark mark='e'/> The goal is learning with guarantees: never much worse than the classical method, often much better.
d2755fe379b5.zh: 第二个前沿是估计。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们看到了独立性假设失败得有多严重。<bookmark mark='b'/>一条研究路线训练模型，用数据本身或已经运行过的查询，去预测结果的大小，捕捉直方图漏掉的相关性。<bookmark mark='c'/>另一条直接学习计划。2019 年的 Neo 用一个从经验中训练出来的神经网络取代了优化器。两年后的 Bao 更谦虚：它保留经典优化器，只逐个查询地学习该给它什么提示。<bookmark mark='d'/>难点在于信任。模型可能以谁都没预料到的方式出错，而一个查询突然从一秒变成一小时，对用户来说比一个一直都有点慢的查询更糟。<bookmark mark='e'/>目标是带保证的学习：从不比经典方法差很多，常常好得多。

a3acba22fa4b.en: The third frontier is checking. <bookmark mark='a'/> How do we know a database delivers the isolation it promises? Run many transactions against it at once, record what each read and wrote, and check the history. <bookmark mark='b'/> In general this is hard: deciding whether a history is serializable is NP-complete, and so, it was shown in 2019, is deciding snapshot isolation, although read committed is easy. <bookmark mark='c'/> The way out is to design the test so that every read reveals which write it saw, for example by appending to lists and reading whole lists. Then the dependency graph of chapter twelve can be built directly and searched for cycles. <bookmark mark='d'/> Elle does exactly this, and Cobra uses a constraint solver; between them they check millions of operations, and they have found real anomalies in many shipped databases. <bookmark mark='e'/> Further out are proofs: verified semantics for SQL and verified rewrites, though in general deciding whether two SQL queries are equivalent is undecidable, a cousin of Part 25's halting problem.
a3acba22fa4b.zh: 第三个前沿是检查。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们怎么知道数据库兑现了它承诺的隔离？同时对它运行许多事务，记录每个读了什么、写了什么，再检查这段历史。<bookmark mark='b'/>一般来说这很难：判定一段历史是否可串行化是 NP 完全的，2019 年又证明了判定快照隔离也是，尽管读已提交很容易。<bookmark mark='c'/>出路是把测试设计成每次读都能显示它看到的是哪次写，比如向列表追加、再读整个列表。这样就能直接构造第十二章的依赖图，再在其中找环。<bookmark mark='d'/>Elle 正是这样做的，Cobra 则用一个约束求解器；两者能检查数以百万计的操作，并在许多已发布的数据库里发现了真实的异常。<bookmark mark='e'/>更远处是证明：经过验证的 SQL 语义和经过验证的改写，尽管一般来说，判定两个 SQL 查询是否等价是不可判定的，它是第25部分停机问题的近亲。

d68b42d9ec8b.en: Six problems at the frontier. <bookmark mark='a'/> Size estimates with provable error bounds, even for queries with many joins. <bookmark mark='b'/> Optimizers that combine ordinary and worst-case optimal joins in one plan, and cost both correctly. <bookmark mark='c'/> Learned optimizers that are guaranteed never to make a query slower. <bookmark mark='d'/> Serializable transactions across continents, at the price of snapshot isolation. <bookmark mark='e'/> Checking isolation levels efficiently on any history, not just ones designed for checking. <bookmark mark='f'/> And databases that drive themselves, choosing and changing their own indexes, layouts and settings. The research problem at the end of this part asks something small and sharp: how few aborts can a serializable snapshot scheduler get away with?
d68b42d9ec8b.zh: 前沿上的六个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>有可证误差界的大小估计，即使对有许多连接的查询也一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>能在一个计划里组合普通连接和最坏情况最优连接、并正确估计两者代价的优化器。<bookmark mark='c'/>保证永远不会让查询变慢的学习型优化器。<bookmark mark='d'/>跨越大洲的可串行化事务，只付快照隔离的代价。<bookmark mark='e'/>在任何历史上高效检查隔离级别，而不只是在为检查而设计的历史上。<bookmark mark='f'/>还有自己驾驶自己的数据库，自己选择和改变自己的索引、布局和设置。这一部分末尾的研究问题问的是一件小而尖锐的事：一个可串行化的快照调度器，最少可以只中止多少次？

1e15f6bd70b4.en: What we built in this part. A relational database: Codd's algebra over tables, the theory of good design, a SQL parser, iterators, four join algorithms whose page counts match their formulas, and Selinger's optimizer, searching subsets instead of orders, with the statistics it relies on and the ways they fail. B-plus trees. Then transactions: serializability and its graph, two-phase locking and deadlock, snapshots and write skew, the isolation levels, and ARIES recovering from five hundred crashes. Column stores, and the Job as one line of SQL.
1e15f6bd70b4.zh: 这一部分我们搭建了什么。一个关系数据库：表上的 Codd 代数，好的设计的理论，一个 SQL 解析器，迭代器，四种页数与公式吻合的连接算法，以及 Selinger 的优化器，它搜索子集而不是顺序，还有它所依赖的统计信息及其失效的方式。B+ 树。然后是事务：可串行化及其图，两阶段锁与死锁，快照与写偏斜，隔离级别，以及从五百次崩溃中恢复的 ARIES。列存储，以及成为一行 SQL 的任务。

a828207367aa.en: Where this comes back. Part 39 stretches transactions across machines, with two-phase commit and Spanner's clocks. Part 43 builds services on top of a database, with idempotent requests and sagas in place of distributed transactions. Part 46 turns the write-ahead log into a stream that other systems follow, and builds warehouses on column stores. Part 47 scales the inverted index to the web. And Part 48 puts shards, replicas and caches in front of a database.
a828207367aa.zh: 它们会在哪里再出现。第39部分把事务扩展到多台机器上，用两阶段提交和 Spanner 的时钟。第43部分在数据库之上构建服务，用幂等请求和 saga 代替分布式事务。第46部分把预写日志变成一条供其他系统跟随的流，并在列存储上建数据仓库。第47部分把倒排索引扩展到整个网络。第48部分则在数据库前面放上分片、副本和缓存。

e9000f0cc963.en: In practice. Start with PostgreSQL; use SQLite inside a program and DuckDB for analysis on one machine. When a query is slow, run EXPLAIN ANALYZE and compare the estimated rows with the actual rows: a large gap means the statistics are stale or the columns are correlated. Index the columns your queries filter, join and sort on, and remember that every index slows every write. Know your isolation level, which is usually read committed, and when an invariant spans several rows, like the doctors on call, use serializable and retry on aborts. And normalize first; denormalize only when you have measured why.
e9000f0cc963.zh: 在实践中。从 PostgreSQL 开始；在程序内部用 SQLite，在单机上做分析用 DuckDB。查询慢时，运行 EXPLAIN ANALYZE，比较估计的行数和实际的行数：差距大，说明统计信息过时了，或者列之间有相关性。为查询用来过滤、连接和排序的列建索引，并记住每个索引都会拖慢每一次写。了解你的隔离级别，通常是读已提交；当一个不变式跨越多行时，比如值班的医生，就用可串行化，并在中止时重试。还有，先规范化；只有在测量出原因之后才去反规范化。

5706dfb950fc.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: give our database histograms, and watch the estimate for the most common word come right. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: how many of serializable snapshot isolation's aborts were really necessary, and how few can any scheduler that sees only read-write conflicts make?
5706dfb950fc.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。任何一道都可以暂停来看。第五道是动手题：给我们的数据库加上直方图，看最常见那个词的估计变得正确。最后一道标着星号，是研究问题：可串行化快照隔离的中止，有多少是真正必要的？任何只看得见读写冲突的调度器，最少能只中止多少次？

e79d9c760137.en: Next time, Part 36: Networks, moving bits. The telephone network reserved a wire for every call; Paul Baran and Donald Davies proposed cutting messages into packets that find their own way. We derive what limits each layer of the Internet, from Shannon's capacity to ALOHA's one over two e, and route packets across a network of our own. Part 36, Networks.
e79d9c760137.zh: 下一次，第36部分：网络，搬运比特。电话网为每一通电话保留一条线路；Paul Baran 和 Donald Davies 提出把消息切成分组，让它们自己找路。我们会推导出互联网每一层的极限，从香农容量到 ALOHA 的二 e 分之一，并在我们自己的网络上路由分组。第36部分，网络。
